definitions.definition: For x in R^n and t>0, Δ_xu(x,t)=sum_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t), component by component. The notation u_t,u_tt,∂_{x_j}u and ∂_{x_j}u_t denotes the corresponding classical partial derivatives on R^n×(0,∞). D_xu is the m-by-n matrix with columns ∂_{x_j}u, and |D_xu|^2 is its Frobenius square sum_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|^2. Vectors have the Euclidean dot product and norm. Spatial integrals are Lebesgue integrals on R^n; boxes carry the restricted Lebesgue measure. int denotes topological interior and 1_A denotes the indicator of a set A.
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+sum_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2, for x in R^n and t>0, with exactly the Euclidean and Frobenius normalization of problem.md:38-46.
For every t>0, E(t)=∫_{R^n} e(x,t) dx. This is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral, used after spatial integrability has been established; there is no factor 1/2.

inputs.statement: For every x∈R^n and t>0, u(x,t)·u_t(x,t)=0 and u_t(x,t)·(u_tt(x,t)-Δ_xu(x,t))=0. Moreover u·u_tt=-|u_t|^2 and u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=-|∂_{x_j}u|^2 for every 1≤j≤n. Every real a satisfying u_tt-Δ_xu=a u at that point equals sum_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2; thus u_tt-Δ_xu=(sum_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2)u.

For every t0>0, put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. There exist a compact C⊂R^n and R>0 with C⊂(-R,R)^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and r∈J. Put Q=[-R,R]^n; its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞. Every positive-order partial derivative of u is zero on (R^n\C)×int J. For each r∈int J the following scalar spatial functions are continuous, bounded on Q, zero outside C, and Lebesgue integrable on R^n: e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, u_t·∂_{x_j}u, ∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for each 1≤j≤n. Consequently e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable for every t>0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary t0>0. N002 supplies integrability of e(·,t0) and all derivative products below, and legitimizes the energy definition D003. N003 gives E'(t0)=2∫_{R^n}u_t·u_tt dx+2sum_{j=1}^n∫_{R^n}∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t dx. Use N004 for each spatial index to obtain E'(t0)=2∫u_t·u_tt dx-2sum_{j=1}^n∫u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx. Linearity for this finite sum and D001 give E'(t0)=2∫_{R^n}u_t·(u_tt-Δ_xu)dx, with all integrands evaluated at t0. N001 says the last integrand is identically zero, hence E'(t0)=0.

argument.text: The positive time t0 was arbitrary. By F001, for every r>0, e(·,r) is integrable and E is differentiable at r with E'(r)=0. This proves all requested analytic assertions, with no assertion at zero.

argument.text: For completeness retain the supplied final conservation statement. Fix s,t>0. If s=t, reflexivity gives E(t)=E(s). If s<t, F002 gives differentiability on (s,t) with derivative zero, and also continuity on [s,t], since E is differentiable at every positive time, including the endpoints. Apply M004 to E extended by zero at nonpositive arguments, derivative function identically zero, and endpoints s,t. It gives 0=(E(t)-E(s))/(t-s), hence E(t)=E(s), since t-s>0. If t<s, use the identical application with endpoints t,s and rearrange. All intervals lie strictly in (0,∞), so the extension never affects any value or derivative under consideration. Thus E is constant on (0,∞). Combining this with F002 proves the exported conclusion, with exactly the original density and normalization.
